audience: Engineers designing/onboarding to an async event-driven system

mode_descriptions.v1_monolith_compat: Transitional: order service still does sync DB write, then emits event. Other services react async.
mode_descriptions.v2_pure_events: Future state: order service emits event only; persistence happens in a downstream projector.

flows.name: Place Order (v1)
flows.purpose: Main user action in the transitional state: synchronous DB write, then the event.

flows.name: Place Order (v2)
flows.purpose: Main user action in the target state: event only, persistence happens downstream.
step_outline: order → kafka : produce order.created (NO direct DB write)
(async) kafka → orderdb : projector writes to read model

flows.name: Billing Reacts to Order
flows.purpose: Async fan-out: billing worker consumes the event and charges the card.
step_outline: kafka → billing : deliver order.created (consumer group: billing)
billing → kafka : produce billing.completed or billing.failed

flows.name: Notification Reacts to Order
flows.purpose: Parallel fan-out: notification worker emails the customer.

flows.name: Shipping Reacts (After Billing OK)
flows.purpose: Shipping waits for billing.completed before reserving inventory.

lessons: Fan-out is hard to show clearly. Each consumer becomes a separate flow rather than parallel arrows in one flow. The flow tab bar makes the parallelism obvious by listing them side-by-side.

The two modes here are MIGRATION states, not deployment environments. This is unusual but valid — modes can be any orthogonal axis as long as the node set stays the same — here only orderdb's label and tech change.

When a mode changes the step SEQUENCE (different from/to or order), it can't be one flow with mode-swapped payloads — every step has one from/to in every mode. Split it into one flow per mode with only_mode (place_order_v1 / place_order_v2): picking either tab switches the mode to match, and switching the mode away falls back to CONFIG.fallbackFlow or the first tab allowed in the new mode (the other place_order flow when its tab comes first). Keep the names parallel so the tab bar reads as one user story: 'place an order'.

Stripe is a single named node (role 'ext', the External color for 3rd-party systems) that only participates in the billing_reaction flow; in every other flow it renders dimmed. Every node referenced by a step must exist on the canvas — don't invent per-flow nodes. Keep externals to the ones that matter; park them in a corner so they don't crowd the mainline. Roles are color groups: the Order service is 'orch' (API / Service), the three consumers are 'compute' — relabel that legend item to 'Worker' so it doesn't read 'Compute/LLM'.
